exemplars.title: Iffy-or-Not: Critically Evaluating Potential Misinformation Using Fallacy Detection and Socratic Questioning with LLMs
exemplars.why: Fallacious spans are persistently highlighted in the source text, while hovering over an individual highlight reveals attached detail, giving a direct and consequential example of the complete mark-trigger-detail structure.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above Paper Plain because it applies the same exceptionally clear two-layer mechanism to evaluative reasoning rather than the more conventional task of defining technical terms.

exemplars.title: Paper Plain: Making Medical Research Papers Approachable to Healthcare Consumers with Natural Language Processing
exemplars.why: Underlined technical terms provide lightweight source-localized flags, and clicking one opens a tooltip containing both its definition and provenance reference, making the interaction unusually explicit and reconstructable.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above Marvista because the evidence identifies the resting indicator, user action, secondary container, and contents more completely, even though its glossary interaction is less novel.

exemplars.title: Marvista: Exploring the Design of a Human-AI Collaborative News Reading Tool
exemplars.why: Answer-bearing sentences are highlighted inline, and hovering over each marked sentence discloses its corresponding question, cleanly staging a per-unit relationship that supports question-guided reading.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above DevTales because both the persistent inline mark and the unit-specific hover disclosure are explicit, whereas DevTales does not establish what, if anything, visibly flags the code at rest.

notes: The final selection follows the top three in the consensus order because they are also the three candidates whose supplied evidence most clearly satisfies the full structural signature; no score was adjusted by more than 0.3. DevTales was considered closely because it is more distinctive than Paper Plain, but its quote does not verify a persistent resting marker. ReviewFlow and DataDive offer consequential verification workflows, yet their excerpts combine several mechanisms or omit the post-click container. Readers should distrust the Iffy-or-Not excerpt's truncated ending and avoid assuming exactly what detail or container appears on hover. Marvista's excerpt establishes that a corresponding question appears but does not specify the popup's visual form or collapse behavior. Paper Plain has the strongest self-contained evidence, although its interaction is highly conventional.
